Subject: Beta Pulse — Deployment topology & SLA alignment

Thanks for taking the time today — quick recap and proposed plan so we have a single source of truth. I captured the key pain points, target goals, and the technical approach we discussed. Please flag anything I missed.

Summary of pain points (what you told us):
- Production latency spikes on chat endpoints during morning peak (p99 observed ~420ms, target <200ms).
- Bursty inference load from web + mobile (peak ~65 requests/sec; baseline ~10 rps) causing hot cache churn.
- Cost pressure: engineering wants to keep steady-state infra small while supporting peaks.
- Data residency: some tier-1 customers require US-only processing and customer-managed key support.

Business goals (aims):
- p99 tail latency <= 150–200ms for conversational endpoints under 95% of daily load.
- Sustainable unit cost: reduce per-token inference cost ~25% vs current setup via batching + KV-caching.
- Deployment window: pilot in staging in 3 weeks; production canary 6–8 weeks.

Technical constraints we discussed:
- Primary model: conversational + retrieval-augmented generation. You are evaluating 13B-class family for response quality; embedding model for search.
- Sequence lengths: typical user prompts ~80 tokens, responses ~120 tokens; occasional long responses to admins (~1k tokens).
- Regulatory: US-only data processing and integration with customer KMS for keys.

Proposed topology (high-level):
- Dedicated deployment in us-west region with two node pools:
  - Burst pool (GPU: H100-preferred or fallback A100) for peak traffic and canary runs.
  - Steady pool (GPU: A10G / T4 depending on quantization) sized for baseline throughput with aggressive KV caching enabled.
- Smart routing policy: steady pool handles baseline; requests exceeding 50 rps shift to burst pool under autoscale.
- KV/prefix cache for common conversational contexts and reranking caches for embeddings to cut redundant passes.
- Canary plan: 5% traffic routed to new model variant with automatic fallback on latency or error-rate regression.

SLOs we recommend (proposal):
- p50 latency: <35ms token gen (interactive).
- p95 latency: <120ms total response time for median interactions.
- p99 latency: target <=150–200ms for 95% of traffic; allow higher for admin/long-response flows under controlled SLA.
- Throughput target: steady-state 10–20 rps; scalable to 80–100 rps with burst pool (sustained bursts >5 minutes will use capacity planning).

Mutual action plan (proposed owners / dates):
- Send security questionnaire (SOC2 + data residency checklist) — Sean (me) — today (attached: security_questionnaire_SA_v2.xlsx).
- Topology sketch for approval — Marissa — 48 hours (attached: beta_pulse_topology_sketch_v1.pdf).
- Staging pilot: schedule with your infra team — Rajiv — target week of Dec 13.
- Procurement kickoff & terms (pricing band for Dedicated) — Procurement contact — target week of Dec 6.

Attachments we added to this thread: call_recording_20261119_1502.mp3 (internal), beta_pulse_topology_sketch_v1.pdf, security_questionnaire_SA_v2.xlsx

3) Introduce procurement contact so we can share draft terms.

Lena — quick technical clarifications from Solutions Eng after review of the sketch and your notes:

- 13B quantized to 4-bit: expected memory footprint ~13–18 GB depending on tokenizer and kv-cache usage. On A10G we expect ~= 2–3 concurrent streams / card at low latency; on H100 you can get higher concurrency and better sustained throughput. For your peak (65–70 rps) with interactive latencies we recommend a mixed pool: 2 H100-backed burst instances and 4 A10G steady instances as a starting point (we'll tune).
- Batching & autoscale: continuous batching helps throughput without hurting p99 if we cap batch wait time to ~8–12ms for interactive flows. We'll instrument dynamic batch caps based on real-time latency windows.
- KV cache strategy: shard cache by customer key and use prefix-caching for the most common 200 tokens of conversation context. That reduces repeated context recomputation and should drop token ops by ~18–25% on our initial estimate.
- Long-response admin flows (~1k tokens): route to a separate job queue to avoid impacting interactive pool. Admin flows will have relaxed p99 targets.
- KMS: we support customer-managed KMS (Cloud KMS, AWS KMS, and enterprise HSM) — for pilot we can do token-level routing so PII requests use the KMS path while other traffic uses Redwood-managed keys. That keeps pilot momentum while meeting your compliance guardrails.

Next technical steps I will own:
- Produce a detailed sizing matrix and expected cost delta for A10G vs H100 options — deliverable by Nov 23.
- Prepare staging canary run plan (traffic split, success criteria, rollback triggers) — deliverable Nov 30.
- Provide a short script for traffic-shape simulation so your infra team can run the profile pre-pilot.

Attachment: beta_pulse_topology_sketch_v1.pdf (diagram + initial sizing).

If helpful, we can book a 45-minute tuning session next Tue/Thu with our perf eng team.
